**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good

- Root cause fixed at the right layer: `step_units::mm_per_unit` reads the unit from the raw AST *before* any geometry (step.rs:46), refuses unreadable or self-contradicting units by name, and keeps millimetres only when no context states a unit — the file's own declared unit is never second-guessed.
- Driving off the `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` references rather than the first `LENGTH_UNIT` in the file is the right call: I checked the fixtures — Milling-test.step carries an unused bare-metre `#166` beside the assigned MILLI `#165`, and the context-driven read skips it correctly (the decision doc names this as considered-and-dropped).
- The scale-after-tessellate argument holds: `shell_facets` derives its tolerances from each shell's own extent, so mesh quality is unit-independent and only the final numbers scale.
- Pathological scale is caught: every measure value is checked finite and positive, chains are depth-bounded (no hang on a cycle), and an overflowed product lands on the pre-existing `all_finite` gate (mod.rs:85) as `ImportError::NonFinite` — refused, never silently imported.
- Prime Directive clean: no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside `#[cfg(test)]`; the one `as f64` cast is an integer STEP value into a scale factor, benign.
- Process all in order: `fix(app):` + `test(app):` conventional subjects, `Changelog:` line, body ends `Fixes #306`, no CHANGELOG.md edit, `docs/decisions/306-step-units.md` follows the per-PR decision-file convention, provenance line on the new module (ISO 10303-41, public standard), all files well under the ~400-line guide (step_units.rs 240, step.rs 195).
- No dependencies, build.rs, scripts or workflow changes — the diff is four source files plus one doc.

## Local results (trial merge with current main `e607ca1`)

Trial merge applied cleanly, no conflicts. Your base was `8b0d784`; main moved since, but nothing in `geometry/import` changed under you.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` (merged tree) | built clean |
| app `--lib` (incl. the 4 `step_units` tests) | 92 passed, 0 failed |
| `--test import` (incl. both new pins) | 22 passed, 0 failed |
| area_controls, area_open, commands_undo, heights_selection, lead_approach, level_links, mill2d_c, pick_agnostic, pocket3d_hsm, rotary_field_parity, shoulder_adaptive, solid_law, wall_arc_entry | 109 passed, 4 ignored, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I ran `mill2d_c` and `rotary_field_parity` on top of your list — both fixtures are millimetre files, both green (`rotary_field_parity` landed on main after your base).

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `SPECIFIC_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` (the 1998-edition form some old AP203 exporters write instead of `GLOBAL_...`) is not scanned — such a file states its unit in a shape this reader won't look at and would silently keep millimetres, exactly the failure mode this PR set out to end. It matches pre-PR behaviour, so nothing regresses, but a follow-up to either resolve it or refuse it by name would close the last silent path. Worth an issue rather than a change to this PR, I think.
- `mm_per_unit` expects the first `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` argument to be a list; a lone unit written as a bare reference (single-element SET, legal Part 21) refuses with "has no unit list". Refusing by name is the safe side, so just noting it in case a real-world export trips it.
- The exact-value pin in `a_step_file_in_millimetres_keeps_its_numbers` (`29.994_477`, 1e-3) is truck-version-sensitive by nature; it agrees with main's reading here, so fine as a regression pin.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
